text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000074 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, but records cover too few high-level claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds across all complexity bands, not just among sicker patients. Low-complexity 99215s in the sample include visits with only acute or nonspecific diagnoses, such as UTI (C0038728, C0038754), URI (C0038762, C0039354) and follow-up Z09 (C0039322, C0039340). That pattern is consistent with upcoding, though the sample cannot be generalized. The provider also has a heavier tail of 4+ condition patients, and the only two documented 99215s (C0038911, C0039025) were high-complexity patients with high MDM supporting the billed level. So part of the excess may reflect genuine acuity. Documentation is too thin to judge because so few 99214/99215 charts came back. The few notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of templated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the Z09 and acute-only visits, to see whether the documented MDM supports level 5."}
